learning_objective: 🎼 Decode the structural framework of Indian music—the three octaves, Pt. Bhatkhande's 10 parent scales (Thaats), the rules of forming a Raga, and their Jatis!

key_vocabulary.hindi_meaning: Octave (A sequential group of 7 pure notes: Mandra, Madhya, and Taar)
Parent Scale (The framework of 7 notes from which Ragas are born; there are 10)
Melodic Framework (A specific combination of notes and rhythm that delights the mind)
King Note (The most important and frequently used note in a Raga)
Classification based on the number of notes used in ascending/descending order (Audav, Shadav, Sampoorna)

main_concepts.simple_explanation: A Saptak is a set of 7 consecutive notes. There are 3 main octaves: 1. Mandra Saptak (Lower/deep octave - denoted by a dot below the note, e.g., .Sa), 2. Madhya Saptak (Middle/normal octave - no dot), and 3. Taar Saptak (Higher octave - dot above the note, e.g., Sa').

To classify thousands of Ragas, Pt. Bhatkhande created 10 Thaats (Parent Scales): Bilawal, Kalyan, Khamaj, Kafi, Asavari, Bhairav, Bhairavi, Poorvi, Marwa, and Todi. A Thaat only has an ascending order (Aroha) and is never sung for entertainment.

A Raga must have at least 5 notes. The note 'Sa' is never omitted. It must possess 'Ranjakata' (the ability to entertain and evoke emotion). Every Raga has a Vadi (King note), Samvadi (Minister note), Anuvadi (Companion notes), and Vivadi (Enemy note).

Based on the number of notes used, Ragas have 3 main Jatis: 1. Audav (5 notes), 2. Shadav (6 notes), and 3. Sampoorna (7 notes). Combining Aroha and Avaroha yields 9 sub-jatis (e.g., Audav-Sampoorna).

The Vadi is the most highlighted note in a Raga, acting as its 'King'. The Samvadi is the second most important note (usually the 4th or 5th note from the Vadi), acting as the 'Minister'. They help determine the time of day the Raga should be sung.

fun_activity.title: 🎹 The 10 Thaat Memory Trick
fun_activity.instructions: Memorize the 10 Thaats of Hindustani Music using a story: 'Bilawal and Kalyan went with Khamaj and Kafi to Asavari to listen to Bhairav, Bhairavi, Poorvi, Marwa, and Todi Ragas!'

exam_tips: 📌 The difference between Thaat and Raga is a highly probable question: Thaat is the generator, Raga is the generated. Thaat is not sung, Raga is sung for entertainment.
📌 Memorize the matrix of the 9 sub-jatis of Ragas (Audav-Audav, Audav-Shadav, etc.) and their note counts.
📌 The Vadi note is often called the 'King' (Raja) and the Samvadi note is the 'Minister' (Mantri).
quick_recap: ⭐ Pandit Vishnu Narayan Bhatkhande introduced the 10-Thaat classification system in Hindustani music.
⭐ Audav uses 5 notes, Shadav uses 6 notes, and Sampoorna uses all 7 notes.
⭐ If a Raga's Vadi note falls in the 'Poorvang' (lower half: Sa to Ma), it is usually sung in the first half of the day (Poorvangavadi Raga).
